sections.heading: The Location: Chiang Rai, Thailand's Northern Capital of Cool
paragraphs: Chiang Rai is one of Thailand's most appealing running destinations: a compact northern city surrounded by mountains, best known for the White Temple (Wat Rong Khun), the Blue Temple, and a climate that's substantially cooler than Bangkok from November through February. [1] A late-January race date catches the tail end of northern Thailand's cool, dry season — morning temperatures in Chiang Rai in January typically range from 12–18°C, which is as good as road-running weather gets in Southeast Asia.

The city itself is flat enough for a road marathon, with the surrounding hills providing backdrop rather than elevation. Chiang Rai is less tourist-saturated than Chiang Mai, roughly three hours north, which means a more local, community-flavoured race experience.

sections.heading: The January Advantage
paragraphs: A late-January race in Chiang Rai is a fundamentally different experience from a mid-year Thai marathon. The cool-season conditions — crisp mornings, low humidity, daytime highs in the mid-to-high 20s — make this one of the more forgiving Thai marathons for runners who aren't heat-acclimated. If you've been put off Thai road races by stories of sweat-soaked 30°C flag-offs, a January northern race is the antidote.
